en: A vision language model is an AI model that
jointly processes visual information and
language so it can answer questions and
reason or generate language about images and
related visual inputs like videos, for
example. Because as you learned in the large
language model lecture, a large language
model is about text in, text out.
A vision language model takes that to the
next level and also is able to understand
images, for example, as input, which is very
powerful because it allows you to ask a
model, hey, what's visible on this image? Or
what's this video about?
And therefore, typical tasks for such a
vision language model include
visual question answering, document
understanding, for example, scans of
documents, chart interpretation, interface
understanding, and image description. Now,
vision models are not new.
Many, many years ago, we already had models
that were able to detect faces on images,
for example. The difference with vision
language models is that they are way more
versatile. They are not there to just have
one specific task, to just detect images or
to just detect faces on images, for example.
But instead, they are there to really
understand an image like you do and answer a
broad variety of questions about that image
potentially.
